description: Security review of a small Flask web application (app.py) for a course lab-submission portal.

items.text: SQL injection in login(): the query is built with an f-string containing the user-supplied username.
Hardcoded secrets in source code: Flask secret_key and/or ADMIN_API_TOKEN.
Weak password hashing: unsalted MD5 used for passwords.
OS command injection in submit(): subprocess.run with shell=True and a user-controlled filename.
Path traversal via unsanitized file names: download() 'name' parameter and/or upload.filename in submit().
Insecure deserialization: pickle.loads on the user-controlled 'prefs' cookie (remote code execution).
Broken access control: /admin/grades only checks that a user is logged in, not that the user has an instructor/admin role.
Flask debug mode enabled (debug=True, bound to 0.0.0.0) in a deployable app, exposing the interactive debugger.
